what: The AWS Wire as it was in its vault when this site was last released: headlines and primary links, each story's edition and dated corrections, the desk's latest release note. The live edition is the vault (v202bla5); this file is the fallback and the index for agents.

wire.title: The AWS Wire
wire.description: Everything AWS announced, filtered by the stack you declare in data/stack.json: what is new, what is insecure, what is being retired, what costs more, and what tooling changed for the services you actually run. Everything else is still listed, as withheld, with the reason.

kind: morning edition and Friday digest: what changed for your stack since Tuesday

latest_release.title: Friday digest: Lambda durable functions grow, a .NET S3 client flaw, and two deadlines unchanged
latest_release.summary: Friday digest. Touched your stack: Lambda durable functions raise their caps to 30,000 operations and 1 MB checkpoints (aws-34) and gain a Go SDK (aws-40); recursive-loop detection now covers EventBridge custom buses (aws-35); Powertools for Lambda (Python) 3.36.0 adds an alpha Auth utility (aws-41); CloudFront gets IPv6 to VPC origins (aws-36); S3 Metadata reaches six more Regions (aws-37); and a .NET S3 Encryption Client padding-oracle flaw, CVE-2026-110310, is fixed in 3.2.2 and 4.0.3 (aws-30; not boto3). AWS says Lambda is unaffected by the 15 Oct kernel bulletin (aws-31). Deadlines: the re:Invent full refund ends today, 16 Oct; Python 3.10 on Lambda ends support on 31 Oct (the runtimes table was re-read and is unchanged); hotel blocks close 5 Nov. Updated: boto3 is now at 1.43.114 (aws-12), Web Functions got a new coverage link and an unresolved question over the 128-concurrent-requests figure (aws-01), and the re:Invent FAQ date was corrected (aws-21). Gaps: the What's New feed was truncated so a few items may be missing, one Bedrock AgentCore item could not be fetched, and CLI and CDK releases past 2.37.13 and 2.273.0 are unconfirmed. Fact-check by a Haiku verifier is in data/factcheck-2026-10-16.json.
